DeepTRACE’s main results table reports **50.3% citation accuracy** for Gemini Deep Research.

However, the accompanying prose reports **40.3%** and labels it “problematic.” The table labels 50.3% “borderline,” consistent with the paper’s threshold where scores below 50% are problematic. This strongly suggests **40.3% is a textual typo and 50.3% is the intended figure**, but the paper is not internally consistent. See [Table 1 and the accompanying results discussion](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.04499#S4).

That release did not occur. As of 27 July 2026:

- Node.js 26.5.0, released 8 July, remains the latest published 26.x version in the [official release index](https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest/).
- There is no official 26.5.1 download, release page, or Git tag.
- Node.js scheduled its next 26.x security release for **27 July 2026**, not 20 July, and has not yet disclosed the vulnerabilities beyond saying the highest severity is **High**. See the [official security announcement](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/july-2026-security-releases).

Consequently, Node.js 26.5.1 has not fixed or addressed any published CVEs yet.

You may be thinking of **Node.js 20.5.1**, released 9 August 2023. It fixed seven Node.js vulnerabilities: CVE-2023-32002, CVE-2023-32558, CVE-2023-32004, CVE-2023-32006, CVE-2023-32559, CVE-2023-32005, and CVE-2023-32003, plus bundled OpenSSL security updates. [Official 20.5.1 release notes](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v20.5.1).
